stories.headline: Wayne Rooney: Bruno Fernandes, Man United players acting like 'babies'
stories.summary: Wayne Rooney has lambasted Manchester United's squad for acting like "babies" and urged Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez to look in the mirror.
stories.body:
Wayne Rooney has lambasted Manchester United's squad for acting like "babies" and urged Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez to look in the mirror.

Fernandes followed Martínez in producing an eye-catching post-match interview on the back of Wednesday's 4-1 defeat at Como in the Champions League.

The result increased the scrutiny on Michael Carrick, who then faced criticism from Fernandes for the game plan in Italy but Rooney has accused the current United captain and Martínez -- who pointed the finger at Jason Wilcox -- of being selfish.

Sources: Carrick to lead Man United against Bournemouth

During an appearance on "The United Stand" podcast, Rooney, who also called for the board to provide clarity regarding Carrick's future, said: "When Martínez came out, I said this is an absolute nightmare because it will rip the dressing room apart. That was the start.

"We've seen it now with Bruno and you're going to see it with more players. The reason why is because them players don't want to take responsibility.

"You can say whether Bruno was right or wrong in what he said, but you have to take responsibility on the pitch, you have to take responsibility as a group of players and there were times when me and Sir Alex Ferguson wouldn't talk, but I'd run through a brick wall for him on the pitch.

"These players, they're selfish. They care about themselves, they don't care about their team-mates, don't care about the manager, about the staff or the fans, they care about themselves.

"If they're not getting what's right for them. They're like babies and just throw their toys out of the pram and go and deflect the blame on to anyone else but themselves. They have to look at themselves.

- Ogden: Who's to blame for Man United mess: Carrick, the players ... Ratcliffe?

- Dawson: Man United were abysmal in Como, but only Carrick who will suffer

"Bruno, he's having probably the worst run of form he's had since he's been at the club and again, it's no coincidence he's putting pressure on someone else because he doesn't want to face it.

"If he looks at himself in the mirror, if Martínez looks at himself in the mirror, all the players... they'll find what is looking back at them is them and it's not good enough."

stories.headline: British teenager Freddie Slater to make F1 practice debut for Audi in Mexico and Brazil
stories.summary: British star Freddie Slater is set to make his Formula 1 practice debut for Audi at the Mexico Grand Prix next weekend.
stories.body:
British star Freddie Slater is set to make his Formula 1 practice debut for Audi at the Mexico Grand Prix next weekend.

The 18-year-old, who became the first driver to be signed to Audi's Driver Development Programme earlier this year, will also be taking part in first practice at the Sao Paulo Grand Prix next month.

Slater has had an impressive run in Formula 3 on his debut season with Trident Motorsport after he stood on the podium eight times in eight races before finishing runner-up to Ugo Ugochukwu in the championship, just 14 points between them.

"Getting behind the wheel of an F1 car at a grand prix weekend is a big moment for me and something I've been dreaming of since I was a kid," Slater said.

"I've learned a lot this year, and these Free Practice outings with Audi F1 Team will be another opportunity to keep gaining on-track experience.

"I'm really looking forward to getting out on track: my focus will be on doing the best job I can, helping the team with its programme and taking as many learnings as possible from both sessions."

- Kimi Antonelli is on the brink of F1 history -- but first, there's a car to wash and pranks to pull

- How Kimi Antonelli can win F1 title at United States GP -- with or without Qatar, Abu Dhabi races

- Christian Horner to Mercedes? Ex-Red Bull boss reveals pre-Toto Wolff approach

Slater has also been promoted to Formula 2 for the 2027 season with Invicta, replacing title leader Rafael Camara, who has recently signed a contract for Haas in F1 for next year.

"We have seen Freddie making great progress throughout recent years, both on and off the track; it is the right time for Freddie to step-up," Audi racing director and head of the development programme Allan McNish said.

"These appearances in Mexico and Brazil will give him valuable experience of a Formula 1 race weekend, and another chance to continue his development before he steps up to Formula 2 next season.

"We are looking forward to seeing him in the R26 and supporting him through these two important FP1 sessions."

stories.headline: Valkyries sense 'urgency' for Game 4 of WNBA Finals vs. Dream
stories.summary: The Valkyries don't want to panic, but they understand what's at stake as they face a 2-1 deficit in the WNBA Finals after being routed by Atlanta in Game 3.
stories.body:
ATLANTA -- The Golden State Valkyries don't want to panic, but they understand what's at stake as they face a 2-1 deficit in the WNBA Finals after being steamrolled by the Atlanta Dream in Game 3.

"We continue to point out the things where we lack discipline and where we lack maybe paying attention to their personnel," guard Veronica Burton said over Zoom on Thursday. "We address that and not overreact but also understand that there is a major sense of urgency, and we can't necessarily wait for anything to change."

Game 4 of the best-of-seven series is Saturday.

Golden State started the series on a high note, using a late run to eke out a Game 1 home victory despite trailing for nearly 30 minutes. Atlanta, however, took Game 2 at Ballhalla, leading by as many as 21, and then protected home court with a 26-point blowout in Game 3.

The nature of the losses has been rather uncharacteristic for Golden State. In those games, the Valkyries have turned over the ball 36 times, resulting in 46 points for the Dream. That's after Golden State averaged just 11.5 turnovers per game in the regular season (fewest in the league) and 10.3 per game in the playoffs before the series.

Atlanta got much of what it was looking for offensively on Wednesday, using a 23-9 run to take control of the game after it was tied at 48 early in the third quarter. The Dream's 97 points were the second most allowed by the Valkyries this postseason; Golden State is 0-8 this year, including playoffs, when allowing 90 or more points.

"An element of it obviously is a little bit surprising in the sense of that is kind of what we hang our hats on, is our discipline, is our composure," Burton said.

Valkyries coach Natalie Nakase said that when the team often thrives when its back is against the wall, especially when players can work as a connected unit.

In these playoffs alone, the Valkyries have stormed back from 16- and 17-point deficits to win games. This 2-1 series deficit, Nakase said Wednesday, is an extended opportunity to do that again through a more aggressive game plan.

"Our players, our staff, we love to come together in these moments," Nakase said. "We get even more connected, get more clarity out of it. Didn't go our way last game, but now we're just focused on the next game. ... This is what brings the best out of us in these moments."

Golden State hasn't lost three games in a row at any point this season.

"It is a long series, so I think we're still very positive," said Kiah Stokes, who won three WNBA titles with the Las Vegas Aces. "We know what we can fix. A lot of it is dealing with ourselves, so we just got to look in the mirror first and then move forward. I think positivity and energy is still high, and we got another chance to steal one on Saturday."

stories.headline: LaMelo Ball obviously traveled on way to 3-pointer, NBA refs confirm
stories.summary: The association that represents NBA referees confirmed that LaMelo Ball took two steps too many and traveled in a widely seen clip from Wednesday night's win over Miami.
stories.body:
MIAMI -- Upon review, Minnesota's LaMelo Ball traveled.

Really, really traveled.

The association that represents NBA referees posted a clip from Wednesday night's game between the Timberwolves and the Miami Heat and clarified -- not that it needed much clarification -- that Ball indeed did commit a violation on his way to a 3-pointer in the second quarter of Minnesota's win.

"For everyone asking, 'how is this legal?' It's not!" the referees' union wrote in a post on X. "He gathers with his right foot on the floor and would be permitted two steps by rule (left-right). He takes four steps after gathering the ball and travels."

Even Ball's brother, seven-year NBA player Lonzo Ball, got the call right moments after the play.

"Travel lmaoooo," Lonzo Ball posted.

Told in an interview with ESPN after the game that his brother made the traveling call, LaMelo Ball -- who was making his Minnesota debut -- still insisted he didn't commit a violation.

"He hatin'. He hatin'," LaMelo Ball said in the televised interview. "See, I gotta give him a call right now, cause with the family, he knows what you're supposed to do. Even if I'm wrong, I'm right. That's how it goes."

Ball's shouldn't-have-counted shot broke what was a 39-39 tie at the time, but in the end it wasn't like the 3-pointer played a big role in the outcome. LaMelo Ball finished the game with 21 points, and Minnesota won 131-106.

stories.headline: Soccer's main characters after UCL Matchday 3: Kane, Van Dijk, El Clasico
stories.summary: Champions League Matchday 3 has come and gone, and we have some Main Character energy coming from Harry Kane, Barcelona and Real Madrid ahead of El Clasico, while Liverpool should worry about Virgil van Dijk's form.
stories.body:
`

By the time they were going for their third straight Champions League title in 2017-18, Real Madrid had mastered the art of easing in. In 2016-17, they finished behind Borussia Dortmund in their group and constantly needed their trademarked, late-game Real Madrid magic to secure points before igniting in the knockout rounds. For the three-peat, they finished second in their group behind Tottenham Hotspur, but mostly rolled in the spring again.

Paris Saint-Germain have certainly learned that you don't have to look your sharpest early on. Two seasons ago, in their first of what is currently a two-year title streak -- and in the first year for the expanded league phase structure -- they narrowly beat Girona in their first match and then lost three of their next four matches before finally starting to click into place in December. They won their next five Champions League matches by a combined 18 goals, knocked off top-seeded Liverpool in penalties in the round of 16 and ... mostly rolled from there.

You can play with fire without getting burned, but Luis Enrique has decided he really doesn't want to. PSG started far better last year, winning four of their first five league phase matches, and this fall they've been all business: After a 6-1 tuneup against Slovan Bratislava to start, they've beaten Manchester City and Barcelona, each by multiple goals. They were winless in their first four matches in all competitions in this campaign, but when the Champions League began, so did their season.

- UCL Power Rankings: Can anyone slow PSG down?

- Talking Points: Man United's mess, PSG lose Kvara, more

- Dawson: Who are Como, the destination club making waves

Along with a 2-2 draw between Arsenal and Bayern Munich, PSG's 4-2 win over Barcelona was the most noteworthy result of Champions League Matchday 3, even if Khvicha Kvaratskhelia's ACL tear cast a bit of a pall on the proceedings. But five teams continued their perfect starts -- PSG, Real Madrid, Liverpool, Aston Villa and Real Betis -- and all of the most likely candidates to win next week's Ballon d'Or made exciting plays.

The league phase keeps rolling, but here are soccer's five main characters as we move past Matchday 3.

Main character No. 1: Harry Kane's closing argument

The voting for this year's Ballon d'Or, which will be awarded this coming Monday, closed a while ago. While the prediction market odds were shifting toward Barca's Lamine Yamal for a while, they appear to have homed in on Bayern Munich's Harry Kane as the likely winner, and justifiably so. He simply had the best year of anyone, winning three trophies, leading England to the World Cup semifinals for a second time and -- oh yeah -- scoring 73 goals with eight assists in 65 total matches. Yamal had only 25 and 20, respectively, in the same period. England teammate (and Wednesday adversary) Declan Rice declared him incredibly deserving, and just in case there was any lingering doubt, Kane put his skill set on display once again in Bayern's 2-2 draw with Arsenal.

The match itself was impacted by absences. Bayern's Michael Olise (red card suspension), Joshua Kimmich (family bereavement) and Jamal Musiala (injury) missed the match, and Arsenal's Bukayo Saka left with injury 10 minutes in. Bayern's Luis Díaz also left with what he later called a minor injury late in the match, and manager Vincent Kompany was even a question mark for the match due to both illness and a hip issue.

These are two of the deepest teams in the world, however, and both lineups still featured plenty of star power. Alphonso Davies ostensibly played on the left wing instead of at left back for most of the evening, and he made the most of the opportunity, getting on the end of a long pass and sending an equalizing goal past David Raya in the 35th minute.

The sender of that beautiful long pass? Kane.

Who both set up and converted the penalty that put Bayern ahead (until Rice's late equalizer)? Kane. That was one of four shots he put on goal, and while Bayern only managed to break Arsenal's defensive line twice with completed passes, Kane was the passer on both. Bayern aren't used to getting anything less than three points at home, but in this case, playing with a short-handed squad against a team that thumped them 3-1 in last year's league phase, a draw was a pretty solid result.

Bayern will visit third-place Freiburg in Bundesliga action on Sunday, and then we'll find out if Kane's Ballon d'Or time has arrived. He would be Bayern's first winner since Karl-Heinz Rummenigge in 1981 (justice for Robert Lewandowski) and the first English winner since Michael Owen in 2001.

Kane isn't a stranger to awards. Name another person who has won the Premier League Golden Boot, the World Cup Golden Boot, Bundesliga Player of the Season and the Millwall Young Player of the Year award and has also been named a member of the Order of the British Empire -- you can't. But between the overbearing presence of Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo over individual awards, and the fact that he has only recently played for a team that regularly wins hardware, Kane has yet to finish in the top three of the Ballon d'Or voting. And now he'd be a deserving winner at 33.

It's a pretty remarkable tale for a player who has spent 15 years honing weaknesses into strengths and becoming a better and better player.

Main character No. 2: Vitinha's perfect role

At a broad level, nothing really went right for Paris Saint-Germain against Barcelona on Tuesday. Three starters had to be subbed off injured in the first hour, and superstar Khvicha Kvaratskhelia tore his ACL. Ferran Torres, thrust into action when Ousmane Dembélé came out after 20 minutes, created three great opportunities, but hit the post once and had two efforts saved. Désiré Doué scored to give the Parisiens a first-half lead, but Xavi Espart equalized early in the second half, and Lamine Yamal, looking as dangerous as ever, equalized for Barca again after PSG got an unlikely goal from Lucas Hernández (his first in over two years).

As ever, however, PSG had Vitinha.

If you told me the Line-Breaking Passes statistic was invented specifically to measure Vitinha's greatness, I'd believe you: He had 15 of them against Barca, and 12 were completed while under pressure from Barca's relentless midfield. He actually led PSG in both passes that broke the attacking line (eight) and passes that broke the midfield line (six), and he trailed only Doue in total carry distance (250 meters) as well. And in the 81st minute, with the buzz from Yamal's goal having not completely worn off yet, Vitinha went into "I'll do it myself" mode.

Vitinha remains the hinge for PSG's absurd successes; considering the injuries and constant shuffling up front, you could make an easy case that he's their most important player. And that just makes me madder at Roberto Martinez.

I covered a majority of Portugal's matches at the 2026 FIFA World Cup, and I was pretty excited about it considering how much I've come to enjoy Vitinha's PSG play; he's a brilliant ball progressor with a take-charge streak, somehow making him a combination of Pedri and Steven Gerrard. But he was mostly ineffective in the World Cup. While he averaged about the same number of touches as he does for PSG, Portugal's refusal/inability to progress the ball with purpose meant that he was mostly working the ball horizontally.

Some players are simply better for club than country, or vice versa, so Vitinha's struggles don't have to mean anything specific. But man, is it hard to believe that; Portugal featured three of Vitinha's PSG teammates (João Neves, Nuno Mendes and Gonçalo Ramos), plus three members of a Manchester City team that loved possession and occasionally sexy ball progression as much as PSG (Rúben Dias, Matheus Nunes, Bernardo Silva). But none of the team's infinite number of creatives seemed to match their club levels and while it makes me a bit of a broken record, it's hard to ignore the other main subplot for Portugal's World Cup disappointment: Martinez's insistence on playing Cristiano Ronaldo up front.

Portugal's attack got consistently gummed up as Ronaldo walked around, slowed the attack down whenever he was on the ball and contributed nothing to pressing structures. Almost insultingly, Vitinha was subbed out of every match and averaged only 76.2 minutes per appearance; Ronaldo finished four of five matches and averaged 88.2 minutes.

Even in the recent international break, with Martinez out and Ronaldo playing a minimal role before his petulant walk-out, Vitinha's role was relatively un-PSG-like. He contributed more in attack, with far more shots and expected assists, more ball recoveries and more line-breaking passes received but far fewer overall touches.

Ronaldo alone wasn't impacting his role, but Portugal was certainly more effective without him. Thank goodness the Ronaldo era is finally over ... right? RIGHT??

Well, whatever. At least we get to see Vitinha in full glory in the Champions League.

Main character No. 3: Virgil van Dijk and Liverpool's ongoing rebuild

Maybe Sir Alex Ferguson's most impressive trait was his ability to regenerate a roster. His vaunted Class of 1992 certainly drove a lot of United's success in the late-1990s and 2000s, but United finished in the top three of England's first division for 21 consecutive seasons and only once went more than one year without a title. (That was at the start of the Roman Abramovich era at Chelsea, when the Blues barged into what had been a two-team title picture with United and Arsenal. United responded to a three-year drought with three consecutive titles.)

As even Pep Guardiola learned, keeping a title-level roster going, without loyalty and age eventually producing a tired lineup -- and without burning out -- is ridiculously hard. For all of Manchester City's spending advantages (legal and otherwise), Guardiola resigned last spring after pulling only a 43% Fergie (nine straight top-threes). After six titles in seven years, staleness overtook City in 2024-25, and they needed a huge burst of January spending to pull off a distant third place in the Premier League race. They improved only marginally last season, though they've started this season beautifully, despite epic noise, under Enzo Maresca.

West of Manchester, Liverpool is pulling off an even more awkward transition. They're on their third manager in four seasons, and of the 16 players who started at least eight matches during their semi-surprising 2024-25 Premier League title run, nine are gone, and three more are at least 30 years old. Dominik Szoboszlai, Ryan Gravenberch, Alexis Mac Allister and Cody Gakpo give them a solid base of players who are both in their prime and have been around a while, but age in both attack and defense forced Liverpool to regenerate, and two summers in, we're still seeing almost frantically up-and-down results.

Their scoring has improved by 23% this season in all competitions, from 1.77 goals per game to 2.18. Two of last season's disappointing signings -- Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz -- have started to contribute at a more consistent level, with six goals and four assists between them. For all the scrutiny piled onto him, Wirtz leads his team in ground duels won (37), chances created (28), shot attempts (25), line-breaking passes received (157), line-breaking passes in the attacking third (26) and ball recoveries (48), and he now has a goal and two assists in his past three matches. Beyond Wirtz and Isak, however, Andoni Iraola's frequently aggressive tactics have produced opportunities for just about everyone in a red shirt: Ten players have scored at least one goal, and 11 have at least one assist.

Liverpool are playing fun ball again and have scored 12 goals in three matches since a disappointing 3-0 loss to Manchester City. They've also allowed three goals in three of their past four matches. Five of their 11 matches this season have featured at least four combined goals. This is great for neutrals, but it's also a sign that defensive fragility is their next issue to address.

That brings us to the Virgil van Dijk conundrum. The Liverpool legend remains a vital cog in buildup play and ball progression -- he's first on the team in touches, passes completed, passes received, progressive carries, progressive passes, line-breaking passes, aerial duels, you name it. He's also 35 and a bit more error-prone, and Iraola's high risk profile means he's getting exposed a bit more in transition.

Tuesday's match against Villarreal began with one of the biggest errors of Van Dijk's Liverpool tenure.

Sergi Cardona scored a beautiful transition goal to put Villarreal up 2-0 before the 30th minute, too, but Liverpool's attacking prowess eventually won out. Mac Allister scored a pair of goals, teenager Rio Ngumoha assisted goals for Ronald Araújo and Mac Allister in probably the best match of his career, and Wirtz put away an eventual 4-3 win in transition.

This was all of Liverpool's upside and downside in the extreme, and it made them more difficult than ever to evaluate. Their moments of brilliance gave them three points after devastating errors dug them a hole. Van Dijk was poor -- "obviously I tried, but it was a bad day at the office personally," he told the media afterward -- but it didn't end up mattering. I'm not sure how much longer this period of Liverpool transition lasts, and I'm not sure how much longer Van Dijk's excellent traits outweigh age, but hey, at least the Reds are entertaining as hell.

Main character No. 4: Sasa and the first-timers

We once again saw plenty of goals in this week's Champions League action -- a delightful 74 in 18 matches, over two per team. Manchester City casually knocked in five without Erling Haaland against AEK Athens, while seven scored four, including Galatasaray in a campaign-saving comeback against Lille, Como in the latest humiliation of Manchester United and Liverpool and Napoli in matching 4-3 wins over Villarreal and Bodø/Glimt, respectively. Hell, five more scored three goals. Aston Villa moved to nine points and 12 goals with a 3-1 win over Viking, and the ever-watchable Club Brugge chugged right along, 3-0, over Lens. Hell, Bayern even coaxed a match with four total goals out of Arsenal.

We're going to focus on someone else, though. While most of these matches will be forgotten six months from now -- hey, I enjoy the league phase perfectly fine, but there's definitely an "endless content with minimal jeopardy" aspect to it -- LASK's win over Sporting CP will end up part of club lore.

LASK won their first Austrian Bundesliga crown in 61 years last spring, and while they've spent plenty of time in the Europa League and Conference League of late, a win over Celtic in August (they came back from 3-0 down after the first leg) qualified them for the Champions League for the first time in, well, 61 years, back when it was the European Cup. They've beaten Inter Milan, Sporting CP, Werder Bremen and other bigger names in previous tournaments, but on Wednesday they scored their first official Champions League win. And a familiar name played a major role.

You may have last seen Sasa Kalajdzic during one of the wildest sequences of the World Cup. After Algeria scored a shocking 100-pass goal to take a late 3-2 lead on Austria in the final matchday, in a match in which both teams would advance with a draw, the stoic Kalajdzic used his 6-foot-7 frame to head in an equalizer moments later. It was his first goal for Austria since overtime in the Euro 2020 round of 16. The guy knows his moments. And in the 63rd minute in Lisbon on Wednesday, he put LASK ahead 2-1. They would lead the rest of the way.

Kalajdzic has suffered three ACL tears in recent years, and he has enjoyed only one season with double-digit goals since he scored 10 for Admira Wacker Amateure in Austria's Regionalliga East 10 years ago. But no one can accuse him of failing to make memories.

Main character No. 5: El Clasico

In the late 2000s, the Premier League's money cannon began to reap dividends. Between 2005-09, English teams took 12 of the 20 spots in Champions League semifinals, six of 10 in the finals and won the title in 2005 (Liverpool over AC Milan) and 2008 (Manchester United over countrymate Chelsea). Sustained brilliance from Manchester United and Arsenal, plus a Roman Abramovich-backed charge from Chelsea, gave England a seemingly permanent place atop the soccer hierarchy.

That dominance came to a (temporary) halt, however, at the hands of two Spanish giants. Between 2009-18, either Barcelona or Real Madrid won seven of 10 Champions League titles, and English teams made only four finals appearances with one win (Chelsea over Bayern in 2012). Barcelona's playing style became the model for nearly every monied team in the world, give or take, and Real Madrid overwhelmed opponents with talent and late-game magic.

In 2026, the Premier League has grown as dominant as ever. Five different English teams have made the Champions League finals since 2019 (three have won), and English teams have won the past two Europa Leagues (it was an all-English final in 2025) and three of the past four Conference Leagues.

Granted, PSG's own financial dominance has conquered the Champions League the past two years -- and handed Barcelona their first loss of the season on Tuesday -- but Spain's dynamic duo might be ready to disrupt England's gravitational pull a bit more. Especially if Yan Diomande is ready to do a little bit more of this.

I'm not sure it's possible to strike a ball any sweeter than that.

Real Madrid were at their most attractive in the second half, getting goals from Arda Güler, Kylian Mbappé and Diomande on their way to a 4-1 romp over RB Leipzig. They've scored four goals in six of their 12 matches this season -- 33 in all -- and Vinícius Júnior hasn't even gotten going yet. They got xG'd to hell in a 1-0 loss to Real Betis in September (20 shots, 3.5 xG, zero goals), and they got Atletico'd in a 2-1 Madrid derby loss, but they've won 10 matches, and a win over Barcelona in the first El Clasico of the season on Sunday would pull them to within three points of the top of LaLiga. For all of the great headlines Barca have earned to start the season, Real Madrid aren't far behind.

Barca have earned those headlines, by the way. Lamine Yamal just played on a losing team for the first time since April 8, and he still managed to do this.

Raphinha missed a month of action after playing the best ball of his life, and Barcelona kept scoring loads of goals without him. Yamal already has 10 goals and 10 assists in all competitions, and Raphinha has 14 and three, respectively. Anthony Gordon, with his three lungs, was born to play for Hansi Flick, while Fermín López, Karim Adeyemi and Gabriel Jesus have combined for 13 goals. And Barca's midfield depth is so ridiculous that Flick was able to bring Gavi and Rodri off the bench on Tuesday. They fell to PSG, and Flick's high-wire style will always leave them a bit vulnerable in the back. But they play the most seductive and watchable ball in the world, and I think they're allowed one loss every six months.

In other words, Sunday's El Clasico (Sunday, 4 p.m. ET, ABC) could be something else.

stories.headline: NHL Tonight: Previews, stats and betting intel for Thursday's dozen games
stories.summary: Get your multi-view ready, hockey fans, it's another busy night!
stories.body:
Regular readers of NHL Tonight know that with it being Thursday there will be a lot of hockey games tonight.

Indeed, with a dozen contests, it's yet another night where it pays to have Power Play on ESPN+, along with a heavy dose of the multi-view option.

Here's a look at what you need to know for each of tonight's 12 contests, including betting info and broadcast details:

Odds are provided by DraftKings and subject to change.

Nashville Predators at Boston Bruins

7 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | BOS -155, O/U: 5.5

There's another new format for the All-Star Game this season -- a round-robin, 3-on-3 tournament with teams composed of players based on nationality. Various players skating in this game could be on the ice in February for that event, including American Olympians Jeremy Swayman and Charlie McAvoy, with Czechia native David Pastrnak joining Team Rest of World.

Is there a case for Steven Stamkos to make Team Canada? The future Hall of Famer has 10 points through eight games, after netting 42 goals last season.

New York Rangers at Toronto Maple Leafs

7 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | NYR -112, O/U: 6.5

If the season was over right now, these are two playoff teams! There are more than 70 games remaining on each team's calendar so let's not draw up the parade routes just yet, but it's notable for the fact that neither was close to a playoff berth in 2025-26.

The Rangers have been the beneficiary of a breakout performance by Dylan Garand, while the Leafs have been paced (unsurprisingly) by Auston Matthews and William Nylander, along with newcomer Kirill Marchenko and 21-year-old Easton Cowan. Who earns the valuable two points out of this one?

San Jose Sharks at Ottawa Senators

7 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | OTT -130, O/U: 6.5

Two of the biggest trades this summer included the Senators: the trade sending Brady Tkachuk to Florida, and the subsequent deal to land Sharks winger William Eklund (using the No. 9 pick from the Panthers in that swap). The Sens were reunited with Brady on Wednesday, but the Sharks will not get to see their old pal William on the ice on Thursday -- he's out several more weeks after ankle surgery.

Nevertheless, the healthy Senators will hope to slow down a potent Sharks attack that knocked off the Canadiens earlier this week.

Anaheim Ducks at New Jersey Devils

7 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | NJ -198, O/U: 6.5

To some degree, both of these teams were expected to be in the playoff picture by season's end. To do that, they'll both need to start stringing wins together. The Ducks went oh-fer on their other stops in the NYC metro area, extending their current losing streak to four games.

The Devils have had some impressive wins lately (4-3 over the Avs, 7-1 against the Rangers), but have also been on the wrong side of lopsided losses to the Sens, Mammoth and Islanders.

Florida Panthers at Pittsburgh Penguins

7 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | FLA -105, O/U: 6.5

If nothing else, Penguins games have been exciting this season. Pittsburgh is scoring 3.30 goals per game, and allowing 3.80; that's fun for everyone! Florida will be playing this game 24 hours after the emotional high of taking on Brady Tkachuk's former teammates in Ottawa. Can they summon a second wind against Sidney Crosby & Co.?

Los Angeles Kings at New York Islanders

7:30 p.m. ET (Disney+/ESPN+/Hulu) | NYI -120, O/U: 5.5

It took seven games, but the Kings are finally on the board with a victory in 2026-27! The defiant 5-2 win was emblematic of what they haven't done much of this season: scoring goals (with just 12 total in the six prior games).

That newfound offense will be put to the test against one of the game's finest netminders, Ilya Sorokin, who is fourth this season in both goals-against average (1.72) and save percentage (.934).

Vegas Golden Knights at St. Louis Blues

8 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | VGK -120, O/U: 6.5

Speaking of scoring, the Golden Knights have two players on the Top-10 scoring leaderboard at this juncture -- Jack Eichel and Mark Stone -- both of whom are on pace to finish with career highs in points.

Standing in their way is Blues goalie Joel Hofer, who got back on track with a 32-save win against Winnipeg on Tuesday following a five-goals-against loss to the Wild.

Winnipeg Jets at Dallas Stars

8 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | DAL -205, O/U: 5.5

Prior to the trade request/holdout/suspension of Connor Hellebuyck, this game had shaped up to be a showdown between two of the top American goalies of this generation, with Jake Oettinger manning the crease for the Stars.

Regardless, there are still two very important points on the line for both the Stars -- who come in on a three-game heater -- and the Jets -- who have lost three straight after a better-than-expected start.

Minnesota Wild at Calgary Flames

9 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | MIN -192, O/U: 5.5

On paper, this one doesn't look too close. But on some nights, the Flames look like they can play with -- and beat -- just about anyone. To wit, their recent wins over the Hurricanes and Ducks.

Or, it could turn out like losses to Colorado (7-3) or Vegas (6-2).

Carolina Hurricanes at Edmonton Oilers

9 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | CAR -115, O/U: 6.5

A potential Stanley Cup Final preview? This matchup has a 2.51% chance of occurring, per Stathletes projections. And while those who like "big markets" might prefer them to be on the biggest stage, there is no shortage of star power in this matchup.

Edmonton's Connor McDavid, Leon Draisaitl and Evan Bouchard -- along with Carolina's Sebastian Aho -- are all among the top point scorers this season.

Utah Mammoth at Seattle Kraken

10 p.m. ET (Disney+/ESPN+/Hulu) | UTA -162, O/U: 6.5

It might be surprising for some to see the Mammoth atop the mighty Central Division standings after 10 games, although their inspired postseason appearance was a clue that something big is being built in Utah.

But the Kraken's hold on the No. 3 spot in the Pacific? That qualifies as a legitimate shock, given what the franchise had done in recent seasons. This contest will be an important one for both teams to continue building their identity as legit contenders in the West.

Detroit Red Wings at Vancouver Canucks

10 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | DET -170, O/U: 6.5

After winning two of their first three games this season, the Canucks have regressed back to essentially where many believed they'd be, and lost their next eight.

The Red Wings are trending in the opposite direction, with at least one point in each of their past five (two wins, and three OT/SO losses). Do both trends continue on Thursday?

stories.headline: St. Louis City beats Columbus in Open Cup final for club's first trophy
stories.summary: St. Louis City won the first trophy in the club's history on Wednesday after defeating Columbus Crew on penalties to lift the U.S. Open Cup.
stories.body:
Backup goalkeeper Ben Lundt made a key save in the penalty shootout of a 120-minute 0-0 tie with the Columbus Crew to help St. Louis City SC win the Lamar Hunt U.S. Open Cup on Wednesday night.

Timo Baumgartl gave St. Louis a 1-0 lead on the first penalty kick and then Lundt dove to his left to get a hand on Santiago Rodriguez's shot that deflected off the post.

St. Louis went 5 for 5 in the shootout, capped by Daniel Edelman's shot down the middle as goalkeeper Nicholas Hagen went the wrong way. Lukas MacNaughton, Chris Durkin and Damion Downs also scored.

St. Louis earned a spot in the 2027 CONCACF Champions Cup after securing the first major trophy in club history.

Columbus was seeking its second U.S. Open Cup title in club history.

Lundt entered the game in the 78th minute after starter Roman Bürki took a knee to the head while making a save. Bürki waved to the crowd while being carted off the field. Lundt came on in relief for his fourth appearance of the season.

It was the first U.S Open Cup final to go to penalties since 2015 when Sporting Kansas City beat the Philadelphia Union. The USOC is open to both professional and amateur clubs, but Major League Soccer teams have dominated the competition for more than two decades.

stories.headline: Way-too-early AFL tiers: There's a clear flag favourite; 'silly season' winners and losers
stories.summary: Who are the 2027 flag favourites? Who are the legitimate contenders? And who should already be booking September holidays? It's our way-too-early edition of AFL tiers.
stories.body:
The 2026 AFL season is done and dusted, but that hasn't stopped ESPN's senior writer Jake Michaels from turning his attention to next year. Who are the 2027 flag favourites? Who are the legitimate contenders? And who should already be booking September holidays? It's our way-too-early edition of AFL tiers!

All of our best footy content, now on Instagram. Follow @espnfooty here!

Your new premiership favourite

1. HAWTHORN

Who knows if the Hawks would have been premiers this year if not for Hugh McCluggage's heroics late in that dramatic preliminary final at the MCG. There's certainly a real argument they would have gone all the way. This side, which is expertly coached by Sam Mitchell, just added Zach Merrett and Ben King to its best 23, two more experienced players desperate for flag success. There won't be many games the Hawks don't start favourite in next year. Even if this club's 2027 season over/under was set at preliminary final weekend, I'd still be taking the over.

Should be great, but there are some questions

2. BRISBANE

3. FREMANTLE

4. SYDNEY

The Lions just completed a remarkable three-peat and it certainly wouldn't have been outrageous for them to hold top spot here. But losing Lachie Neale and Chris Fagan -- arguably the two most important pieces of the club's modern-day dynasty -- cannot be underestimated. How do they fill those seismic gaps? The Dockers were the dominant team of the home and away season and if we played out the last four minutes of the Grand Final 100 times they probably win 99 of them. Instead, Fremantle has to spend all offseason dwelling on the greatest missed opportunity in club history. How do they respond in 2027? As for the Swans, who are always somewhere around the mark, nobody can really be sure what to expect after the Pullman Hotel saga. So many fascinating questions.

Silly season winners

5. GEELONG

6. WESTERN BULLDOGS

7. CARLTON

8. COLLINGWOOD

Each of these teams will be counting down the days until the 2027 season after drastically improving their lists during the trade and free agency window. The Cats landed the dynamic Toby Greene, significantly upgraded their ruck department with the singing of Rowan Marshall, and bolstered their defensive stocks with Jordan Ridley. The Bulldogs scored the biggest prize of all in Zak Butters, but they were also able to pry away Jordon Butts from the Crows, a much needed acquisition to what's been a shaky defence. The Blues will go into next season with Joel Amartey, Lachie Whitfield, and almost certainly father-son talent Cody Walker, while the Magpies added dual Brownlow medallist Lachie Neale and 2024 Coleman Medal winner Jesse Hogan.

Silly season losers

9. MELBOURNE

10. ADELAIDE

While a bunch of teams we'd expect to be in the fifth-to-10th range clearly improved their best 23, the Demons and Crows did nothing of the sort. Adelaide literally brought in nobody and will have to deal with the loss of key defender Jordon Butts, who departed as a free agent for the Bulldogs. Melbourne did sign several names, but do we think any of Zane Duursma, Will McLachlan, and Bodie Ryan can be needle movers in 2027? But hey, these were two sides I was down on this year and both ultimately outperformed expectations. Perhaps they do have it all figured out...

It's now or never

11. GOLD COAST

12. NORTH MELBOURNE

13. ST KILDA

If not now, then when? The Suns rocketed to co-flag favouritism this time last year after signing Christian Petracca and Jamarra Ugle-Hagan. They ultimately won just nine games and finished 13th on the ladder. Disastrous. Damien Hardwick is under serious pressure to get more out of this list. Meanwhile, the Kangaroos haven't played finals in a decade, but there's some newfound optimism after the senior coaching appointment of highly regarded Jaymie Graham and the signing of Nick Blakey, the biggest name the club has attracted in a decade. The Saints also need to show something early in 2027 or Ross Lyon could be on his way out ... again! But the real worry is not doing enough to ensure star midfielder Nasiah Wanganeen-Milera signs on.

It's going to be another long year

14. PORT ADELAIDE

15. GWS

16. WEST COAST

17. RICHMOND

18. ESSENDON

Perhaps I'm being a tad harsh on Port, who were pretty competitive this year. But at the end of the day we're taking Zak Butters out of a side that won just seven games. The Giants lost four of their best players in Toby Greene, Jesse Hogan, Lachie Whitfield, and Kieren Briggs, and will be relying heavily on their younger talent next year. And then there's the Eagles, Tigers, and Bombers -- three teams that combined for just nine wins this year. We all expect these sides to be somewhere around the bottom of the ladder.
